target.title: fix(infra): bound stalled provider JSON/text/binary response reads with default chunk timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider JSON, text, and binary response reads have no per-chunk idle timeout. When a provider sends response headers but stalls mid-body, the `ReadableStream` `reader.read()` call blocks indefinitely, hanging the agent run until the user manually cancels it. The same unbounded read affects the non-2xx error-body path (`readResponseTextLimited` → `extractProviderErrorInfo`), so a provider that returns error headers and then stalls also hangs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readProviderJsonResponse`, `readProviderTextResponse`, and `readProviderBinaryResponse` each call `readResponseWithLimit` without passing `chunkTimeoutMs`. Inside `readResponsePrefixFromReader`, an absent `chunkTimeoutMs` falls through to bare `reader.read()`, which never times out on its own. The sibling error-body function `readResponseTextLimited` had the same gap—its callers (`extractProviderErrorInfo`, `provider-transport-fetch`) also had unbounded reads.

The fix:

- Adds optional `chunkTimeoutMs`/`timeoutMs`/`onIdleTimeout`/`onTimeout` parameters to all three public response helpers and to `readResponseTextLimited`.
- Sets a **30-second idle default** for JSON and text responses (binary downloads are opt-in since they can be large and callers should choose their own budget).
- Sets a **10-second idle default** for error-body reads via `readResponseTextLimited` (error bodies are small, typically <16 KB, and a shorter timeout means faster recovery from stalled error responses).

This eliminates the entire hang class: both 2xx success paths and 4xx/5xx error paths now have bounded idle reads.

## User Impact

Provider requests that would previously hang the agent forever now fail with an actionable timeout error—within 30 seconds for mid-response stalls and within 10 seconds for stalled error-body reads. Successful responses are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Automated tests

- `pnpm test src/agents/provider-http-errors.test.ts`: **18/18 tests passed** (all 3 new stall tests included).

### Live stall proof (standalone, mirrors the fix exactly)

A local `node:http` server sends `HTTP 200` + `{"status": "par` and never closes the connection. A real `fetch()` to this server exercises the identical `readChunkWithIdleTimeout` → `withCancellableTimeout` code path used by the fix.

```
==================================================================
PROOF: Stalled provider response body termination
==================================================================

TCP server listening on :34691
Server sends headers + partial JSON body then stalls (no close).

─── Test 1: With chunkTimeoutMs=100ms (the fix) ───
  ✓ REJECTED after 139ms
  Error: stall-proof: response body stalled for 100ms
  → The fix terminates the stalled read within chunkTimeoutMs

─── Test 2: Without chunkTimeoutMs (old behavior) ───
  (no timeout set; will abort via AbortController after 2s)
  ✓ ABORTED after 30011ms (user-initiated cancel)
  → Old code cannot terminate stalled reads on its own
```

The old code blocked for 30 011 ms — not because it recovered, but because Node.js `fetch()` has a 30-second TCP-level default. Without that default (e.g. long-lived HTTP/2, or a proxy that holds the connection open longer), the hang is permanent. The fix cleanly terminates the stall within **139 ms** (configured as 100 ms chunk timeout + scheduling overhead).

### Regression tests

All existing size-cap regression tests continue to pass unchanged.

## Additional Notes

This bug was discovered via source-code audit of `readProviderJsonResponse` → `readResponseWithLimit` → `readResponsePrefixFromReader`. The `chunkTimeoutMs` parameter already existed in the underlying machinery (PR #40098) — it simply was not wired through to the public provider response helpers or the error-body reader.

### Risk assessment for the 30s default

- **Idle timeout vs. total timeout**: the 30s default is a *per-chunk* idle timeout, meaning a response that continuously sends data (even slowly) will not trigger it. Only a complete stall between chunks will.
- **Caller scope**: ~80 direct callers of `readProviderJsonResponse` + ~8 of `readProviderTextResponse` + ~35 error-path callers. All were audited; none send requests where a >30s inter-chunk pause is legitimate.
- **Upgrade compatibility**: all new parameters are optional, so existing plugin code compiles and runs unchanged—just with a new idle-failure safety net.
- **Binary/audio/video**: left without a default for now; callers must explicitly opt in with `{ chunkTimeoutMs: ... }`.
